purpose: Test calibration/ghost plausibility for three preselected terrestrial-frame comb groups; preserve original dispositions and no automatic assignment.

measurements.native_A_and_B: Retain every covering order, evaluate each native wavelength polynomial; median-filter high-pass residual window31 native pixels.
measurements.comparison: At same observed wavelength, linearly interpolate B high-pass onto A wavelength. Pearson correlation of finite samples in fixed +/-1.5 Angstrom. Also retain local spectral peak spacings (find_peaks distance5,prominence2 times residual MAD) descriptive, not detection threshold.
measurements.raw_visual: For reference exposures, retain wider raw patches around every overlapping A order: +/-250 native-dispersion pixels and +/-80 raw cross-dispersion pixels; plot curves for A/B orders from header geometry. Use existing validated raw orientation; retain local mapping uncertainty. No best-shift optimization or fitted ghost-path selection in initial analysis.
measurements.hypothesis_limit: Direct same-wavelength B correlation cannot prove/refute a reflected ghost that maps another order/position. FP configuration + near published broad affected ranges + terrestrial repetition strengthen only mechanism plausibility; actual ghost identification needs geometry/calibration.

published_prior.summary: Reported reference-fiber FP ghost comb around3822/3851 Angstrom; broad range, not exact-line ID. Known before new local flux inspection.
